description: Monitoring and modeling sound-side erosion near Oregon Inlet, North Carolina to support feasibility level transportation planning is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Elizabeth Sciaudone, North Carolina State University (ncsu.edu). NCDOT Research Project 2020-09 “Monitoring and modeling sound-side erosion near Oregon Inlet to support feasibility level transportation planning” used field observations, numerical modeling, fragility curves, and engineering analysis to (1) assess the hydrodynamics and erosion processes near Oregon Inlet, (2) estimate the potential for roadway failure based on marsh conditions, and (3) evaluate potential erosion ... Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: field measurements; marsh shoreline erosion; flood vulnerability; rapid response; shoreline assessment. Published 2022-10-21. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
